newsitem.title: USA: Hawaiian Electric Q2 bank oper net rises.
newsitem.headline: Hawaiian Electric Q2 bank oper net rises.

text.p: Hawaiian Electric Industries, Inc. Tuesday reported net income for the three months ended June 30, 1997 of $19.8 million, or $0.63 a share, compared with $21.4 million, or $0.71 a share, in the same period of 1996.
For the six months ended June 30, 1997 net income was $39.5 million, or $1.27 per share, compared with $40.2 million, or $1.34 per share, in the same period of 1996.

"The strong operating performance of our savings bank was more than offset by lower results at the electric utility and other segments," said Robert Clarke, president and chief executive officer. "Our utility kilowatt hour sales have been impacted by cooler weather and the soft tourism industry."

The company said temperatures on Oahu through June were cooler than last year, resulting in lower kilowatt hour sales due partly to less air-conditioning usage. Visitor arrivals in Hawaii through May were down 0.5 percent compared with the same period of 1996.

Electric utility operating income during the quarter declined 7 percent to $40.4 million compared with $43.4 million in the same quarter of 1996. Operating income for the six months was $79.0 million versus $82.1 million in the same period last year. Kilowatthour sales for the quarter and six months were down 1.7 percent and 0.5 percent, respectively, from the same periods of 1996.

Higher maintenance expenses and depreciation from plant additions also contributed to the decline in operating income. The recent twelve month return on average common equity for the Oahu utility declined to 10.7 percent compared to 11.8 percent for the twelve months ended June 30, 1996.

HEI's savings bank subsidiary reported a 20 percent increase in operating income to $12.2 million for the quarter compared with $10.2 million in the same quarter of 1996. Operating income for the six months was $24.5 million versus $20.2 million in the same period last year. Results in 1997 are up due to increased net interest income, lower deposit insurance premiums and expense controls, partly offset by larger additions to the provision for loan losses. The bank's interest rate spread -- the difference between the yield on earning assets and cost of funds -- was 2.97 percent for the six months versus 2.82 percent in the same period last year. The bank's average earning assets are up 6 percent year-to- date versus 1996's first half. The bank's return on average common equity for the six months ended June 30, 1997 improved to 12.6 percent, compared to 10.9 percent in the same period last year.

In May, HEI's savings bank subsidiary signed a definitive agreement to acquire substantially all of the Hawaii deposits of Bank of America, FSB, most of its branches and certain of its Hawaii-based loans. "The acquisition of Bank of America's Hawaii operations has the potential to add up to 50 basis points to HEI's return on average common equity in 1998 and up to another 50 basis points in 1999," HEI's president and CEO, Robert F. Clarke, has said. An application to approve the acquisition was filed with the Office of Thrift Supervision on July 10, 1997, and work necessary to complete the acquisition is proceeding as scheduled. It is currently anticipated that approximately $160 million of new capital will be infused by HEI into its savings bank to meet regulatory capital requirements related to its increased asset size following the acquisition. No utility funds will be used to finance the acquisition.

Operating income at the company's maritime freight transportation and passive investment subsidiaries was more than offset by operating losses and expenses at the corporate parent and the real estate and new independent power subsidiaries. Prior year results reflected a pretax gain of $1.1 million from a sale of land in downtown Honolulu by the real estate subsidiary.
